messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 page: gpu-capacity-exhaustion. Autoscaler reports repeated failures, queue exploding, and elevated 429s. Paging on-call: raj.

raj: Oncall here. grabbing quick context. Which region? any recent deploys?

jess: region=us-west-2. No deploys from infra in last 30m. Spike started ~09:50Z. Charts: https://graf.redwood/prod/gpu/us-west-2 (link). Queue depth from 20 -> 620 in ~3m. 429s spiking to 35%.

liam: Autoscaler errors show provider quota + subnet IP exhaustion intermittently: 
```
2026-03-15T09:52:12Z ERROR provider: allocate_node failed: provider_quota_exceeded: GPU quota 0/16
2026-03-15T09:52:25Z ERROR provider: allocate_node failed: insufficient_subnet_ips
```
Also saw `scale_up` attempts throttled by control-plane with `rate_limited_provisioning` flag.

raj: so two issues: provider quota and control-plane rate-limiter for provisioning API. That explains the delay. 429s might be coming from token-bucket hitting hard. jess can you show rate-limiter config?

jess: current rate-limiter policy: `global: 1000r/s, tiered: enterprise=600r/s (bucket=1200), pro=200r/s, free=50r/s`. But bucket refill for all tiers is uniform and low for long bursts. During this spike, free/pro tiers hit bucket and got 429s; enterprise got prioritized but some traffic still dropped because control-plane was also rejecting provisioning calls.

sre-ops: I can make a quick change: (a) temporarily increase refill rate for all tiers by 3x, (b) add a short-lived allowlist for customers with active support entitlements, and (c) reduce penalty period for dropped tokens from 5s -> 1s. Patching now: 
```
PATCH /svc/rate-limiter/config
{ "patch": [{"op":"replace","path":"/refill_rate","value":"*3"}, {"op":"add","path":"/allowlist","value":["org-acme","org-fitcloud"]}]} 
```

sre-ops: applying patch. rolling to 3 control-plane replicas to reduce provisioning API rate-limit.

infra-bot: control-plane replicas: 2 -> 5 (rolling update kicked off).

jess: after changes: 429s for enterprise -> 1.2%, pro -> 8%, free -> 41%. Queue depth decreased to ~240 but still elevated.

support-eng: customer impact: multiple tickets from mid-tier customers complaining about "generation aborted (429)". Enterprise customers reported slower responses but few errors. I've posted an interim status to affected customers and set expectations.

liam: autoscaler still blocked by provider GPU quota. I filed an expedited quota request with provider with priority contact. ETA uncertain ~20-40m. In parallel, we can try: (1) preemptible/spot GPU instances in another AZ, (2) fallback to smaller quantized models to reduce GPU pressure, (3) reassign idle capacity from staging or dev pools. Thoughts?

raj: prioritize (2) and (3) immediately, start (1) as fallback if quota update takes too long. Who can change routing for model fallback?

sre-ops: I will flip routing for standard/pro tiers to send 60% of requests to quantized-4b (low mem) when queue depth > 300. Command: `svc-router set-fallback --tier=pro --pct=60 --model=quantized-4b --cond='queue>300'`. Executing now.

sre-ops: routing change applied.

jess: also enabling per-customer burst credits: granting +200 token burst to orgs with active SLA to avoid noisy-neighbor drops while we add capacity. 

liam: drained noncritical pools and reclaimed 3 GPUs (drained `sandbox-gpu-pool`). Running: `./poolctl drain sandbox-gpu-pool --grace=30s --evict=true`.

liam: reclaimed +3 GPUs, combined with re-routing and refill tuning we see queue down to 110 and 429s falling to 6% overall.

support-eng: customers updated: enterprise all clear; pro customers seeing reduced errors; free tier still hit with retries. I'm triaging open tickets and escalating two that are high impact.

raj: note for post-incident: token-bucket bucket_size and refill policy are too punitive for sudden bursts and amplify provider-side provision lag. We should add a control-plane health check: if autoscaler reports >2 consecutive failed provisions, automatically relax token-bucket parameters (with audit trail) and enable cross-region spillover for short window.

jess: agreed. I'll create an RFC for emergency autopilot rules. On immediate next steps: keep routing and refill changes for 15 minutes, then gradually roll back to observe stability.

infra-bot: provider quota request status: pending -> acknowledged. Support engineer assigned. ETA updated to 23m.

liam: provider responded: can allocate but need to switch to different instance family (a100->a10x). That implies perf differences but better availability. Do we want to run a mixed-pool strategy?

raj: yes, enable mixed-pool. Configure autoscaler to accept a10x as fallback: `autoscaler.set_allowed_instance_types([a100,a10x])`. Also lower per-node min-concurrency to allow more pods per fallback node.

sre-ops: applied mixed-pool config. provisioning a10x nodes now.

jess: monitoring: queue depth trending down to ~40, 429s ~0.8% across all tiers. latency back to baseline for critical customers.

support-eng: posting another customer update: "We experienced elevated 429s and longer latencies due to regional GPU provisioning limits which coincided with conservative rate-limiter settings. Engineering implemented temporary refill and routing changes and reclaimed capacity from noncritical pools. We will follow up with a post-incident summary."

raj: created incident tracker INC-2026-03316, assigned postmortem owners: jess (rate-limiter tuning), liam (autoscaler/provider fallback), sre-ops (automation for emergency bypass).

incident-bot: Severity set to mitigated. Please add postmortem link when available.

infra-bot: 6 fallback nodes (a10x) became ready at 10:12Z -> `node-provisioner: ready nodes 6/6`.

raj: handing off to next oncall jess at 10:20Z. I'll stay reachable for follow-ups. Good work everyone. :thumbsup:

jess: closing thread after handoff. Action items in INC-2026-03316. Will schedule 45m postmortem tomorrow.
